records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] readLength's bounds check compares the declared length against the total input size (limit), not the remaining bytes (limit - count), so it only rejects lengths that overshoot the entire buffer. For a nested element near the end of a corrupted signature, a length that overruns the current element but stays under the total buffer passes readLength and fails later in read() with a generic EOF IOException (or reads sibling bytes as content), losing the 'corrupted stream - out of bounds length' diagnostic and making malformed-signature errors harder to attribute; no test covers the overlong-length path.
records.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` the bounds check is `if (length >= limit) { throw ... }`, where `limit = bytes.length` (total input size) and it does not account for how many bytes have already been consumed (`count`). records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AuthzClientCryptoProvider registers itself as a classpath-wide CryptoProvider service while 14 of its 19 methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, and getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default KeyStore provider rather than BouncyCastle. Any application that has authz-client on its classpath alongside another CryptoProvider of lower order (any third-party provider with order < 100, which is all pre-existing ones given they lack order() — though those already fail per the interface break; or a future low-order one) silently routes all crypto through a provider whose getPemUtils/getSignature/getCertificateUtils throw. Within authz-client itself, any code path beyond ECDSA signature conversion — e.g. PEM parsing of a client's signing key or the JWT client-credential flow — now calls into these stubs and crashes at runtime. records.issue_text: [BUG] This diff silently deletes the fail-fast 'multiple crypto providers on the classpath' IllegalStateException contract from CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, replacing it with order()-based silent selection, without any explicit acceptance of that behavioral change to server-side code. Previously, a misconfigured server classpath containing both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider (or elytron) threw an IllegalStateException at startup, telling the operator exactly which providers conflicted; now it silently picks the highest-order provider and only logs 'Ignored crypto providers' at DEBUG level.
